To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the FIV protease chimera 6s-90S has five replacements mimicked from HIV PR and a 6th mutation that was acquired during selection, and that the structure of this chimera with the HIV PR inhibitors darunavar and lopinavar reveals the role of a 90s loop, residue 98, and residues 37, 55, 56 and 59 in conferring drug sensitivity.

(1) a chimeric fiv/hiv protease was designed and engineered to be sensitive to HIV protease inhibitors, (2) the structure of this chimera was solved with two HIV protease inhibitors bound, and (3) the results of this study provide insight into how to engineer HIV protease inhibitor resistance into a feline immunodeficient virus.
(1) The FIV PR chimeric structure reveals a novel mode of binding for DRV and LPV; and (2) The chimeric Fiv PR structure is a template for the development of novel anti-HIV drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis for drug and Gag substrate specificity exhibited by the 6s98S PR.
the design of a FIV PR chiméra which is sensitive to HIV PR inhibitors.
understanding the structural basis of drug and substrate specificity in the FIV PR chimers and how these chimeras can be exploited as a platform for drug development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a chimeric PR has been engineered that confers sensitivity to HIV protease inhibitors but retains the ability to process the FIV Gag polyprotein.
the chimeric Feline immunodeficiency Virus (FIV) Protease (PR) 6s- 98S has been engineered that confers sensitivity to HIV PR inhibitors darunavri (DRV) and Lopinavir (LVP).
the chimeric 6s-PR is a useful tool for the study of FIV and HIV proteases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the chimeric FV/HIV PR exhibits a drug-binding mode similar to that of the HIV PR, but with a different conformation of the flap, a flexible 90 s loop and a Pro to Ser mutation at position 98, all of which are required to support infectivity.
the 6s98S FIV chimera is a valuable tool for studying HIV PR inhibitor resistance.

the 6s FIV PR chimeras are useful tools to study the structure-function relationships for the HIV PR and its inhibitors and to understand the structural basis for substrate specificity exhibited by PR enzymes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to design a chimeric PR that supports infectivity and is highly sensitive to a specific drug.
it is possible to create a FIV PR chiméra with HIV PR inhibitor sensitivity and Gag processing ability.
it is possible to generate a FIV PR with a high level of drug resistance that is also highly efficient at processing Gag substrates and supports infectivity.
